question: What is the primary definition of the rectal route of drug administration?

options.A: Inhaling drug vapors directly into the lungs
options.B: Applying medicated cream onto the outer skin
options.C: Swallowing medicine with a large glass of water
options.D: Inserting medication directly into the rectum

explanation: The rectal route simply means placing a drug directly into the rectal cavity for local or systemic effects. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h1)

question: When is a nurse most likely to consider using the rectal route for a patient?

options.A: When the patient prefers a fast topical skin effect
options.B: When the patient needs a daily multivitamin tablet
options.C: When the patient cannot take medications by mouth
options.D: When the patient has a mild headache and can swallow

explanation: If oral intake is blocked due to vomiting, unconsciousness, or swallowing difficulties, the rectal route serves as a practical alternative. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which condition makes the rectal route unsafe because of a high risk of bleeding?
explanation: Low platelet counts mean any trauma to the rectal lining can lead to serious, hard-to-stop bleeding. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why should you avoid giving rectal medications to a patient who has active rectal bleeding?

options.A: The patient will automatically develop an allergic reaction to the drug
options.B: The medication can worsen mucosal damage and might be washed away
options.C: The drug will bypass the liver entirely and cause immediate toxicity
options.D: The rectal sphincter will permanently lock shut and trap the medicine

explanation: Active bleeding or severe diarrhea stops the drug from being absorbed properly and can hurt the already irritated tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of administering drugs through the rectum?

options.A: It can be used effectively when a patient is actively vomiting
options.B: It guarantees 100 percent predictable absorption every time
options.C: It is always the preferred choice for alert adult patients
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any hand hygiene

explanation: When oral drugs cannot be kept down due to vomiting, the rectal route ensures the patient still receives necessary treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is one well-known disadvantage of giving medications rectally?

options.A: Immediate destruction of red blood cells
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the anal sphincter

explanation: Because of stool, different blood flow rates, or early expulsion, rectal drugs don't always absorb as steadily as intravenous medications. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h3)

question: How does drug absorption in the lower rectum affect metabolism?

options.A: It sends all medications directly to the stomach
options.B: It destroys the active ingredients instantly
options.C: It forces the drug to be stored in the kidneys
options.D: It bypasses the liver's first-pass metabolism

explanation: Lower rectal veins carry the drug straight into the general circulation, skipping the quick breakdown by the liver that oral pills face. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h4)

question: What common physical thing inside the rectum can block a drug from working well?
explanation: Stool in the way prevents the suppository from touching the bowel wall so it can melt and absorb properly. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the typical physical shape of a rectal suppository?
explanation: Suppositories are molded into rounded, tapering shapes designed for smooth and comfortable insertion into the anal canal. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h5)

question: How do standard suppositories release their medicine once inside the body?

options.A: They melt or dissolve at internal body temperature
options.B: They require digestive enzymes from the stomach to melt
options.C: They are absorbed whole without changing form
options.D: They dissolve instantly when exposed to room air

explanation: They are specially made to stay firm at room temperature, but melt quickly once they meet internal body heat. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why should you check if a patient has recently passed stool before giving a suppository?

options.A: Stool presence guarantees that the drug will be absorbed twice as fast
options.B: A full rectum can block the medication from contacting the mucosal wall
options.C: Bowel movements prevent the nurse from wearing disposable gloves
options.D: Empty bowels mean the patient is allergic to the prescribed drug

explanation: If the rectum is full of stool, the suppository won't touch the lining properly, reducing drug absorption. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h6)

question: What type of lubricant should you always use when inserting a rectal medication?
explanation: Water-soluble lubricants help the suppository slide in smoothly without hurting delicate tissues or damaging gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which patient position is standard and most appropriate for rectal medication administration?
explanation: Sims' position (left lateral with the top leg flexed) naturally exposes the anus and follows the anatomical curve of the lower intestine. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h7)

question: A patient asks why they need to stay lying down for 15 minutes after getting a suppository. What is your best response?

options.A: To help the digestive system push the drug up into the stomach
options.B: To allow the blood pressure to drop safely back to normal levels
options.C: To ensure the patient falls asleep quickly and rests comfortably
options.D: To prevent the medication from being pushed out before it dissolves

explanation: Staying flat gives the medicine time to melt and absorb into the lining instead of sliding right back out. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h7)

question: What should you do if a patient pushes out a suppository right after you insert it?

options.A: Inspect the stool, check the status, and consult the prescriber for a repeat dose
options.B: Immediately force a second suppository into the rectum without checking
options.C: Assume the full dose was already absorbed and document successful administration
options.D: Scold the patient for failing to hold the medication inside the bowel

explanation: If it comes out whole before melting, the dose is lost, and you must check with the prescriber before trying again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h8)

question: What can happen during rectal insertion if you forget to use a lubricant?
explanation: Without lubricant, the friction can easily scrape and injure the delicate rectal lining. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h8)

question: When is the best time to document a rectal suppository in the patient's records?

options.A: Immediately after the procedure is completed
options.B: Before gathering the supplies from the cart
options.C: At the end of the entire nursing shift
options.D: Only if the patient complains of pain later

explanation: Charting right away keeps your records accurate and prevents medication errors. Great job keeping up with your duties! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h9)

question: Which of these details is NOT necessary to chart after giving a rectal medication?

options.A: Any local discomfort or side effects noted
options.B: The patient's favorite hobby or pastime
options.C: The exact time and date of administration
options.D: The specific name and dose of the drug

explanation: Personal hobbies have nothing to do with clinical charting. Always focus on the drug name, dose, time, and patient response! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h9)
